nodes.label: COMP201 Software Engineering
nodes.description: This is the central topic for the COMP201 learning platform, connecting the key software engineering concepts covered in the module.

nodes.label: Requirements Engineering
nodes.description: Requirements engineering focuses on discovering, analysing, documenting, and validating what a software system should do.

nodes.label: Functional Requirements
nodes.description: Functional requirements describe the services and behaviours the system must provide.

nodes.label: Non-Functional Requirements
nodes.description: Non-functional requirements describe qualities such as usability, reliability, performance, and security.

nodes.label: Software Processes
nodes.description: Software processes describe how software is developed, tested, delivered, and maintained.

nodes.label: Waterfall Model
nodes.description: A linear development model where each stage is completed before the next begins.

nodes.label: Agile Development
nodes.description: An iterative and flexible approach to software development focused on collaboration and responsiveness to change.

nodes.label: System Modelling and UML
nodes.description: System modelling uses diagrams and abstractions to represent software systems and their behaviour.

nodes.label: Use Case Diagrams
nodes.description: Use case diagrams show interactions between users or external actors and the system.

nodes.label: Class Diagrams
nodes.description: Class diagrams show classes, attributes, methods, and relationships in object-oriented design.

nodes.label: Object-Oriented Design
nodes.description: Object-oriented design structures software around objects, classes, inheritance, and encapsulation.

nodes.label: Inheritance
nodes.description: Inheritance allows one class to derive properties and behaviours from another.

nodes.label: Encapsulation
nodes.description: Encapsulation keeps data and behaviour bundled together and protects internal state.

nodes.label: Architectural Design
nodes.description: Architectural design defines the high-level structure of a software system and how components interact.

nodes.label: Client-Server Architecture
nodes.description: A distributed architecture where clients request services and servers provide them.

nodes.label: Layered Architecture
nodes.description: A structure that separates a system into layers with distinct responsibilities.

nodes.label: Project Management / Risk / Estimation
nodes.description: This area covers planning, cost estimation, scheduling, and risk analysis in software projects.

nodes.label: Risk Management
nodes.description: Risk management identifies possible project problems and plans actions to reduce their impact.

nodes.label: Effort Estimation
nodes.description: Effort estimation predicts the time, resources, and cost needed for software development.

nodes.label: Petri Nets
nodes.description: Petri nets are a formal modelling technique used to represent concurrent and distributed systems.

nodes.label: Use Cases / Case Studies
nodes.description: Use cases and case studies apply software engineering concepts to realistic scenarios and system interactions.
